title: Sarah Salois, PhD
text: I am a marine ecologist by training with a passion for collaboration. The crux of my research aims to bring the knowledge and data of the fishing community into the scientific process to support the management of our local ecosystems. This can look like developing new data streams with industry partners or building new data products to leverage the vast amount of data the fishing community collects. My work explores the links between oceanographic conditions and species dynamics across important life history stages.

title: Sarah Salois
text:
A little more about me …
Marine Ecologist        Fisheries Biologist   


My Research Pillars:

Cooperative Research: Building strong, collaborative partnerships between the fishing industry and science to improve trust and management outcomes.
Integrated Ocean Data: Integrating a variety of data including in-situ subsurface data, satellite data, and oceanographic model outputs to better understand our marine ecosystems.
Data Accessibility: Developing high-quality visualizations and data products that return insights directly to the folks on the water.




Background
I started at NOAA Fisheries at the Northeast Fisheries Science Center in collaboration with SMAST UMASS Dartmouth as a CINAR Postdoctoral Fellow looking at the oceanographic drivers of the Northern Shortfin Squid (Illex illecebrosus). Knowing very little about the squid fishery in the Northwest Atlantic, necessitated that I talk with commercial squid fishermen in our region. I also had a lot to learn about the underlying mechanisms in our extremely dynamic ocean, connecting me with local oceanographers. Through this opportunity to listen and learn from this amazing group of people, I quickly developed a deep passion and respect for Cooperative Research.
I have since expanded my research portfolio to include other commercially important species including:

Longfin Squid(Doryteuthis pealeii)
Golden Tilefish (Lopholatilus chamaeleonticeps)


Prior to working in the fisheries world, I was modeling metacommunity dynamics to better understand the interplay of abiotic and biotic drivers in marine ecosystems. I used mathematical models, computer simulations and statistical analyses to explore potential vulnerabilities of ecosystems in an era of global change. You can read more about that research here.
